notes: Account: Polaris Edge Systems — supply-chain/last-mile logistics provider; heavy need for low-latency decisioning at edge hubs.
AE notes: strong bias toward on-prem/VPC Dedicated solution with cross-region reserved pools. Wants predictable throughput/cost for peak events (holiday surges).

Use-case summary: real-time chat for driver support (chat), high-recall product embeddings for match/recommend, reranking for routing decisions. Priority: chat latency first, then throughput for embeddings batch jobs.

Performance targets (customer stated): p95 <= 120ms for small-chat tokens; p99 target debated (customer wants p99 < 300ms but legal pushing for stricter SLA). Throughput steady-state ~500 qps with burst to 1200 qps during peak windows.

Reserved GPU planning notes: customer engineering proposes dedicated pools in 3 regions (us-east1, us-west2, eu-west1) with regional headroom ~20% to allow graceful failover + autoscale buffer. Asked for example sizing: 24x A100 equiv per region initially, ability to scale to 40x for Black Friday style bursts.

Failover policy discussed: hot-active in primary, warm-standby in secondary region for chat low-latency paths; cold replicas for large-batch embeddings. Wants routing policy that prefers local region but can shift traffic if latency SLOs are at risk.

SLA negotiation: Polaris legal requested explicit throughput guarantees (tokens/sec) for Dedicated pool and credits for downtime > 99.95% SLA. Redwood must clarify how fallback to hosted variants affects SLA and billing during failover.

Security/compliance: mandatory SSO/SAML, KMS integration with customer HSM, audit logs retained 12 months, EU data residency for customer EU tenants. Compliance team will run SOC2 + ISO27001 checklist (drive link above).
POC timeline: kickoff 2026-02-15 (env access granted), benchmark run 2026-02-25 (baseline), reserved pool test 2026-03-02 (sustained load + failover drills), exec readout 2026-03-09 (VP Eng present).

POC results summary (internal): chat p95 at 110ms in us-east at 80% load; cross-region failover increased p95 to ~220ms — acceptable for non-critical flows, not for SLA'd driver chat. Need routing optimizations + warm-standby to meet p99 goal.
Quote from VP Eng (Amanda Ruiz): 'We need deterministic latency under 150ms for driver-facing flows. Anything that spikes beyond that will erode adoption.'

Cost sensitivity: mid-high. Willing to pay premium for predictable reserved capacity if there is clear failover and routing behavior. Wants cost breakdown per-token + per-reserved-GPU to present to finance.
